items.stem: Define the term 'sensor'.
items.answer: An input device that measures a physical quantity, such as temperature or light, and sends the reading to the computer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the key idea; 1 mark: further detail or a correct example. Model: An input device that measures a physical quantity, such as temperature or light, and sends the reading to the computer. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a sensor does not control the device it is monitoring.
items.answer: A sensor is only an input device that measures a quantity; the microprocessor compares the reading with a preset value and sends signals to an actuator to make changes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark sensor measures/input only; 1 mark microprocessor decides/actuator acts. [2]

items.stem: Explain why sensor readings are taken at regular intervals rather than continuously.
items.answer: The computer processes digital samples; regular sampling gives enough data to see changes while limiting the amount of data stored and processed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark discrete samples; 1 mark enough detail without excess data. [2]

items.stem: Engineers at Pioneer Insurance in Manila are fitting sensors to a new building. Describe what is meant by an actuator and give an example.
items.answer: An output device that performs a physical action in response to a signal, e.g. motor, valve, pump, heater switch.
items.markingKey: 1 mark description; 1 mark example. [2]

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets, a supermarket chain in Lima, is installing a computer system to monitor conditions in its storage rooms. (a) Give two advantages of using sensors rather than human readings. (b) Describe what is meant by an actuator and give an example.
items.answer: (a) Readings taken 24 hours a day; more accurate; at exact intervals; in dangerous places; staff freed for other work. (b) An output device that performs a physical action in response to a signal, e.g. motor, valve, pump, heater switch.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark each, max 2. [2] (b) 1 mark description; 1 mark example. [2]

items.stem: Nadia is designing an automatic system for the greenhouses of Vista Estate Agents near Lisbon. Evaluate whether Vista Estate Agents should replace manual checks by staff with an automatic sensor-based monitoring system.
items.answer: Points for: continuous, accurate readings; works in dangerous places; staff freed; immediate alerts. Points against / limitations: cost of sensors and installation; sensors can fail or drift and need calibration; staff may lose skills; reliance on power and network. Conclusion: automatic monitoring is usually worthwhile if readings are frequent or the environment is hazardous, with periodic human checks.

items.answer: The temperature sensor sends readings via an ADC; the microprocessor compares each reading with the preset range; if too low it switches the heater on (and closes windows); if too high it switches the heater off and opens windows via a motor; this repeats continuously.

items.stem:
This algorithm controls a heater in a greenhouse. Temp is the temperature in °C. At the start, Heater is "ON".
REPEAT
    INPUT Temp
    IF Temp < 18 THEN
        Heater ← "ON"
    ELSE
        IF Temp > 25 THEN
            Heater ← "OFF"
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    OUTPUT Heater
UNTIL SystemOff = TRUE
The inputs for Temp are: 28, 27, 21, 17. Complete a trace table showing the value output after each input.
items.answer: OFF; OFF; OFF; ON
items.markingKey: 28 → OFF; 27 → OFF; 21 → OFF; 17 → ON (1 mark each). [4]

items.stem:
This algorithm controls a compressor in a cold store. Temp is the temperature in °C. At the start, Compressor is "OFF".

    IF Temp > -16 THEN
        Compressor ← "ON"
    ELSE
        IF Temp < -20 THEN
            Compressor ← "OFF"
        ENDIF
    ENDIF

UNTIL SystemOff = TRUE
The inputs for Temp are: -16, -18, -16, -20, -19. Complete a trace table showing the value output after each input.

items.stem:
This algorithm controls a compressor in a cold store. Temp is the temperature in °C. At the start, Compressor is "OFF".
REPEAT
    INPUT Temp
    IF Temp > -16 THEN
        Compressor ← "ON"
    ELSE
        IF Temp < -20 THEN
            Compressor ← "OFF"
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    OUTPUT Compressor
UNTIL SystemOff = TRUE
The inputs for Temp are: -18, -15, -14, -22. Complete a trace table showing the value output after each input.
items.answer: OFF; ON; ON; OFF
items.markingKey: -18 → OFF; -15 → ON; -14 → ON; -22 → OFF (1 mark each). [4]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Describe how a microprocessor controls the temperature in a greenhouse. (b) Explain why a DAC may be needed in a control system.
items.answer: (a) The temperature sensor sends readings via an ADC; the microprocessor compares each reading with the preset range; if too low it switches the heater on (and closes windows); if too high it switches the heater off and opens windows via a motor; this repeats continuously. (b) Some actuators need an analogue signal (e.g. to vary motor speed), so the digital output from the microprocessor must be converted.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark per step, max 4. [4] (b) 1 mark actuator needs analogue; 1 mark converts digital output. [2]
